headline: Majors rally into overbought momentum while shorts liquidate heavily; Bitcoin dominance holds and whales accumulate.
paragraphs: The market crossed higher today with all seven tracked assets gaining ground on the day. Bitcoin rose 5.09 percent to 67,980, Ethereum climbed 8.42 percent to 2,077, and even laggards like BNB and Cardano moved up low single digits. Total market cap grew 4.51 percent to 2.39 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance sits at 57 percent. The regime picture is split: Ethereum alone trades above its 200-day simple moving average, while Bitcoin, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano all sit below it. No golden crosses have formed. This is a relief bounce against a backdrop of structural weakness, not a trend reversal.

Momentum has spiked sharply into overbought territory across the board. Bitcoin's RSI-14 stands at 70.3, Ethereum at 74.5, and Solana at 68.4. In the overbought range, these readings tell you the move is real but also compressed, leaving less runway before a retest. All six major assets with momentum readings show MACD above signal line, so the short-term acceleration is synchronized. What is notable is the absence of divergence: price and momentum agree on direction today, which means the rally lacks the internal warning sign of a top. That said, RSI in the 70s across multiple large-cap assets with no trend confirmation from the 200-day is the kind of snapshot that stops traffic in a risk-off market. Cardano's RSI sits at 49.2 and its MACD is below signal, making it the laggard even in a broad up day.

Derivatives positioning reveals acute stress in short positions. Over the last two hours, Bitcoin saw 1,600 liquidations totaling 74.3 million on the short side versus only 2.7 million on longs. Ethereum liquidations ran 33.3 million in shorts versus 5.6 million in longs. Even smaller assets show the same skew: Solana had 10.4 million in short liquidations over 22 hours, XRP 2.5 million in shorts over 18 hours. Funding rates across all major perps sit at 0.01 percent per eight hours, annualizing to roughly 11 percent. That rate is moderate and stable, not extreme. The long-to-short ratios are elevated across the board: Bitcoin at 1.1, Ethereum at 1.12, Solana at 1.49, and Doge at 4.4. This suggests crowded long positioning in the riskier names, and today's snap higher liquidated traders who were short into the move. Open interest remains substantial, Bitcoin at 2.12 billion and Ethereum at 1.33 billion, so capital is still engaged despite the directional reset.

Whale activity and institutional flows point in opposite directions, which is the tension worth watching. Over the last 24 hours, 104.7 million in Bitcoin exited exchanges, all from OKEx, while 189.9 million in USDT entered Binance. The Bitcoin movement off exchange is a classic accumulation signal; the stablecoin inflow to Binance is a dry powder move that can precede either a bid or a dump depending on what follows. Over the last five sessions, ETF flows have been positive: Bitcoin saw 238.4 million net inflow over five days with only two same-direction sessions, and Ethereum took 115.6 million over five days with two same-direction sessions. Yesterday's single-day ETF flows were 189.3 million in Bitcoin and 71.4 million in Ethereum. The weekly whale net has swung from +1.15 billion two weeks ago to -69.99 million most recently, a sharp reversal. The stablecoin float is 306.5 billion, down 0.51 percent on the month, implying neither flush nor buildup of dry powder at scale.

The Fear & Greed index reads 46, labeled Fear, within a 30-day range of 25 to 46. The crowd is still nervous even as price moves higher. This is classic disbelief in a bounce. Spot ETF flows remain bid, but they are only two days into positive direction. Bitcoin's realized volatility sits at 28.8 percent and Ethereum's at 41 percent, elevated but not panic-level. The network itself is quiet: Bitcoin fees are 1 satoshi per byte, difficulty is flat with 445 blocks to retarget, and the mining infrastructure shows no distress.

The setup to watch is whether the long liquidations ease or intensify into the next session. Bitcoin is 45.5 percent below its 12-month high of 124,739, Ethereum is 56.9 percent below 4,817, and Solana is 67.2 percent below 247. All three sit well off cycle peaks, meaning downside technical support is sparse. If funding flips negative or the long-to-short ratio on smaller assets like Solana rolls over, that would signal the rally has lost its bid. Conversely, if whale accumulation in Bitcoin deepens and ETF inflows remain positive for three or more consecutive sessions, the floor is being tested differently. For now, read it as a short squeeze into overbought momentum, not a regime break.
